note: Constitutional and legal designation. The shortened compound 'ჯანდაცვა' is accepted in common prose and media.
Frontline outpatient clinical services.
State insurance coverage system in Georgia.

'პრიზნაკი' is a Russianism; correct medical term is 'სიმპტომი'.
Recognizable complex of symptoms.
Formal medical conclusion. 'დიაგნოსტიკა' is the examination process, not the finding.
Methods and procedures used to identify medical conditions.
'ნაზნაჩენიე' is a Russianism; correct Georgian is 'დანიშნულება'.
Official document authorizing dispensing of prescription drugs.
'ლეკარსტვო' is a Russianism; correct Georgian is 'მედიკამენტი' or 'წამალი'.
Antimicrobial substance. Singular after numerals: '2 ანტიბიოტიკი'.
Class of medication used specifically for treating viral infections.
'ობეზბოლივაიუში' is a Russianism; correct Georgian is 'ტკივილგამაყუჩებელი'.
'პრივივკა' is a Russianism; correct Georgian is 'ვაქცინა' (substance) or 'აცრა' (inoculation).
Administration of a vaccine. Synonym: აცრა.
Process whereby a person is made immune or resistant to an infectious disease.
Physiological capacity to resist pathogen infection.
Blood protein counteracting specific antigens. Singular after numerals.
Invasion of organism body tissues by disease-causing agents.
Submicroscopic infectious agent replicating inside living cells.
Microscopic single-celled organism.
'ვასპალენიე' is a Russianism; correct Georgian is 'ანთება'.
'პროფილაქტიკა' is an obsolete Sovietism in general health policy; standard modern term is 'პრევენცია'.
Post-treatment restorative medical care.
Admission to hospital for clinical inpatient treatment.
Medical treatment requiring stay in a hospital ward.
Medical treatment without overnight hospitalization.
'სკორი' is a Russianism (скорая); official term is 'გადაუდებელი სამედიცინო დახმარება' or 'სასწრაფო დახმარება'.
Specialized critical care unit. Colloquially: რეანიმაცია.
Invasive clinical operation. Synonym: ოპერაცია.
'ნარკოზი' is colloquial; medical prose uses 'ანესთეზია' (ზოგადი/ადგილობრივი).
'დავლენიე' is a Russianism; correct Georgian is 'არტერიული წნევა' or simply 'წნევა'.
Clinical laboratory terminology; 'სისხლში შაქარი' is acceptable in informal dialogue.

Routine laboratory test of urine parameters.
Clinical chemical analysis of blood serum constituents.
Acronym 'MRI' or full Georgian title. 'ემერტე' is a Russianism (МРТ).
'კატე' is a Russianism (КТ); write in full or use 'CT'.
Colloquially: რენტგენი.
'უზი' is a Russianism (УЗИ); correct terms are 'ულტრაბგერითი გამოკვლევა' or 'ექოსკოპია'.
'ვრაჩი' is a Russianism; standard Georgian is 'ექიმი'.
'ლეჩაშჩი ვრაჩი' is a Russianism; correct Georgian is 'მკურნალი ექიმი'.
'მედსესტრა' is a Russianism; standard Georgian is 'ექთანი'.
Hospital assistant supporting ward sanitation and patient care.
'ბალნოი' is a Russianism; standard Georgian is 'პაციენტი'.
Long-lasting medical condition.
Disease characterized by sudden onset and rapid progression.
'ზარაზნი' is a Russianism; correct Georgian is 'გადამდები' or 'ინფექციური'.
Disorders of the heart and blood vessels.
'სახარნი დიაბეტი' is a Russianism; correct Georgian is 'შაქრიანი დიაბეტი'.
'ზლოკაჩესტვენი' is a Russianism; correct medical term is 'ავთვისებიანი სიმსივნე'.
'დაბროკაჩესტვენი' is a Russianism; correct medical term is 'კეთილთვისებიანი სიმსივნე'.
Secondary malignant growth spreading away from primary site.
Drug treatment using powerful chemicals to destroy cancer cells.
Cancer treatment using high doses of ionizing radiation.
Hypersensitive immune reaction to foreign substances.
'პაბოჩნი ეფექტი' is a Russianism; correct Georgian is 'გვერდითი მოვლენა'.
'პროტივაპაკაზანიე' is a Russianism; correct Georgian is 'უკუჩვენება'.
'პაკაზანიე' is a Russianism; in clinical context the correct term is 'ჩვენება'.
'დოზაჟი' is a clumsy Russian/French loanword; correct Georgian is 'დოზირება'.
'პერედოზირება' is a Russianism; correct Georgian is 'გადაჭარბებული დოზა'.
Physical wound or damage inflicted upon the body.
'პერელომი' is a Russianism; correct Georgian is 'მოტეხილობა'.
'უშიბი' is a Russianism; correct Georgian is 'დაჟეჟილობა'.
'აჟოგი' is a Russianism; correct Georgian is 'დამწვრობა'.
'ატრავალენიე' is a Russianism; correct Georgian is 'მოწამვლა' or clinical 'ინტოქსიკაცია'.
Strict isolation imposed to prevent the spread of infectious disease.
Widespread occurrence of an infectious disease in a community.
Epidemic of infectious disease that spreads across entire continents or worldwide.
